 DES MOINES, Iowa — The annual Affordable Care Act Open Enrollment period began Nov. 1, giving Iowans without employer-sponsored insurance a chance to sign up for individual health coverage.
 The Iowa Insurance Division said consumers can compare plans, check for federal subsidies and enroll through HealthCare.gov or by calling 1-800-318-2596. The enrollment window runs through Jan. 15, 2027.
 "Even if you currently have a plan, the networks, formularies and rates change each year," said Iowa Insurance Commissioner Doug Ommen. "We strongly encourage all Iowans to actively review their options rather than relying on automatic renewal."
 The deadline to enroll for coverage starting Jan. 1, 2027 is Dec. 15, 2026. Plans selected between Dec. 16, 2026 and Jan. 15, 2027 will take effect Feb. 1, 2027.
 After Jan. 15, 2027, Iowans can only enroll or switch plans if they qualify for a Special Enrollment Period due to life events like marriage, loss of employer coverage, birth of a child or relocation. The low-income year-round Special Enrollment Period for households at or below 150% of the Federal Poverty Level has been removed for plan year 2027.
 Before choosing a plan, the division said consumers should verify their preferred doctors, clinics and hospitals remain in-network and that essential prescription medications remain on the plan's formulary. Financial assistance through Advance Premium Tax Credits is available through HealthCare.gov based on projected household income. The only way to get the premium tax credit is through HealthCare.gov or a certified enrollment partner's website.
 Iowans who don't actively select a plan by the end of open enrollment may be automatically re-enrolled into their existing plan or an alternate similar plan if their prior carrier has adjusted offerings. The division warned consumers to watch out for unsolicited marketing and scam websites posing as the official exchange. Official marketplace enrollment occurs exclusively through HealthCare.gov .
 Iowans who previously held individual plans with Medica must select a new carrier during the open enrollment period. Medica exits Iowa's consumer market effective Jan. 1, 2027.
 Consumers should use zip code information or the Iowa county when searching for plans. To locate certified assisters and licensed brokers, visit healthcare.gov/find-assistance . For questions about insurance licensing, carrier complaints or market conduct in Iowa, contact the Iowa Insurance Division at 515-654-6600 or visit iid.iowa.gov .
 Medicare beneficiaries don't enroll through HealthCare.gov . Iowans eligible for Medicare can enroll through medicare.gov or by calling Medicare at 1-800-633-4227.
